description: Jurisdiction profiles for INHERIT consumers — locale, currency, professional terminology, courts, and timelines

_metadata.source: Compiled from official government sources per jurisdiction
_metadata.disclaimer: This data is provided for interoperability purposes. It does not constitute legal, tax, or financial advice. Users must verify independently before relying on these figures for official purposes.
_metadata.deprecationPattern: Individual entries within this file may carry deprecated: true, deprecatedAt, deprecatedReason, and supersededBy fields. Deprecated entries are retained for historical reference and audit trail purposes. Applications should filter to non-deprecated entries for current data.

GB-ENG.name: England & Wales
GB-ENG.testamentaryFreedom: Broad testamentary freedom, but dependants may claim reasonable financial provision under the Inheritance (Provision for Family and Dependants) Act 1975.
GB-ENG.probateCourtName: Probate Registry (Family Division of the High Court)

GB-SCT.name: Scotland
GB-SCT.testamentaryFreedom: Limited by legal rights (jus relictae/jus relicti and legitim), which reserve fixed shares of moveable estate for the surviving spouse and children.

US.name: United States (federal/general)
US.testamentaryFreedom: Generally broad, but most states protect surviving spouses via elective share statutes. Rules vary significantly by state; community property states differ from common law states.

US-CA.name: California
US-CA.testamentaryFreedom: Community property state — the surviving spouse automatically owns half of community property. The testator may freely dispose of their separate property and their half of community property.
US-CA.deathRegistrationBody: California Department of Public Health, Vital Records

US-NY.name: New York
US-NY.testamentaryFreedom: Common law state with an elective share — the surviving spouse may claim the greater of $50,000 or one-third of the net estate regardless of the will.
US-NY.deathRegistrationBody: New York State Department of Health, Vital Records

US-TX.name: Texas
US-TX.testamentaryFreedom: Community property state — each spouse owns half of community property. Texas also protects the homestead, which cannot be devised away from a surviving spouse or minor children.
US-TX.deathRegistrationBody: Texas Department of State Health Services, Vital Statistics

CA.name: Canada
CA.testamentaryFreedom: Varies by province. Common law provinces allow dependant relief claims; Québec follows a civil law system with a patrimony regime protecting spouses.

AU.name: Australia
AU.testamentaryFreedom: Broad testamentary freedom, but all states and territories allow eligible persons to make family provision claims against the estate.
AU.probateCourtName: Supreme Court (Probate Division, varies by state)
AU.deathRegistrationBody: State/Territory Registry of Births, Deaths and Marriages

NZ.name: New Zealand
NZ.testamentaryFreedom: Constrained by the Family Protection Act 1955 and the Property (Relationships) Act 1976, which protect spouses, children, and other dependants.
NZ.deathRegistrationBody: Department of Internal Affairs, Births, Deaths and Marriages

IE.name: Ireland
IE.testamentaryFreedom: The surviving spouse has a legal right to one-third of the estate (or one-half if no children). Children may apply under Section 117 of the Succession Act 1965 if not adequately provided for.

FR.name: France
FR.testamentaryFreedom: Heavily restricted by forced heirship (réserve héréditaire). Children are entitled to between one-half and three-quarters of the estate depending on the number of children.

DE.name: Germany
DE.testamentaryFreedom: Limited by Pflichtteil (compulsory portion), which entitles close relatives (spouse, descendants, parents) to half of their intestate share in cash.
DE.probateCourtName: Nachlassgericht (probate court, part of the Amtsgericht)

ES.name: Spain
ES.testamentaryFreedom: Restricted by forced heirship (legítima). Under the common Spanish Civil Code, two-thirds of the estate is reserved for descendants. Rules vary by autonomous community (e.g. Catalonia, Basque Country, Navarra).

IT.name: Italy
IT.testamentaryFreedom: Restricted by legittima (forced heirship). The reserved portion varies: one-half for one child, two-thirds for two or more children, plus a share for the surviving spouse.
IT.deathRegistrationBody: Ufficio di Stato Civile (municipal civil registry)

NL.name: Netherlands
NL.testamentaryFreedom: Children have a right to a compulsory portion (legitieme portie) equal to half of their intestate share, payable as a monetary claim.

JP.name: Japan
JP.professionalTerm: 司法書士 (shihō shoshi, judicial scrivener) / 弁護士 (bengoshi, lawyer)
JP.testamentaryFreedom: Restricted by iryūbun (遺留分), a statutory reserved portion for spouse, children, and lineal ascendants equal to one-half of the intestate share (one-third for ascendants only).
JP.probateCourtName: 家庭裁判所 (katei saibansho, Family Court)
JP.deathRegistrationBody: 市区町村役場 (shikuchōson yakuba, municipal office)

SG.name: Singapore
SG.testamentaryFreedom: Non-Muslims have broad testamentary freedom. Muslim estates are governed by Islamic inheritance law (farāʾiḍ) administered by the Syariah Court, with fixed shares for heirs.

MY.name: Malaysia
MY.testamentaryFreedom: Non-Muslims have broad testamentary freedom. Muslim estates follow Islamic inheritance law (farāʾiḍ), with distribution governed by Syariah courts.
MY.probateCourtName: High Court (Civil Division) / Syariah Court for Muslims

IN.name: India
IN.testamentaryFreedom: Hindus, Buddhists, Sikhs, and Jains governed by the Indian Succession Act or Hindu Succession Act have broad testamentary freedom. Muslim personal law applies fixed shares (farāʾiḍ) and limits bequests to one-third. Rules vary by religion and state (e.g. Goa follows Portuguese civil code).
IN.probateCourtName: District Court / High Court (varies by state; probate mandatory in some states only)
IN.deathRegistrationBody: Municipal Corporation / Gram Panchayat (under the Registration of Births and Deaths Act)

CN.name: China (mainland)
CN.professionalTerm: 律师 (lǜshī, lawyer) / 公证员 (gōngzhèng yuán, notary)
CN.testamentaryFreedom: The Civil Code (2021) provides relatively broad testamentary freedom, but the testator must reserve a necessary share for heirs who lack the ability to work and have no source of income.
CN.probateCourtName: 人民法院 (rénmín fǎyuàn, People's Court)
CN.deathRegistrationBody: 公安局 (gōng'ānjú, Public Security Bureau) / 民政局 (mínzhèngjú, Civil Affairs Bureau)

KR.name: South Korea
KR.testamentaryFreedom: Restricted by yurubun (유류분), a statutory reserved portion equal to one-half of the intestate share for direct descendants and spouse, and one-third for other heirs.

HK.name: Hong Kong SAR
HK.testamentaryFreedom: Broad testamentary freedom under common law, but dependants may apply for reasonable financial provision under the Inheritance (Provision for Family and Dependants) Ordinance.
HK.deathRegistrationBody: Births and Deaths General Register Office (Immigration Department)

TW.name: Taiwan
TW.testamentaryFreedom: Restricted by tèliúfèn (特留分), a compulsory portion reserving one-half of the intestate share for direct-line descendants and spouse, and one-third for other heirs.
TW.probateCourtName: 地方法院 (dìfāng fǎyuàn, District Court)
TW.deathRegistrationBody: 戶政事務所 (hùzhèng shìwùsuǒ, Household Registration Office)

VN.name: Vietnam
VN.testamentaryFreedom: Broad testamentary freedom, but certain heirs (minor children, parents, spouse, and disabled dependants) who are excluded from the will are entitled to two-thirds of an intestate share.
VN.deathRegistrationBody: Ủy ban nhân dân xã/phường (Communal People's Committee)

TH.name: Thailand
TH.professionalTerm: ทนายความ (thanāi khwām, lawyer)
TH.testamentaryFreedom: Broad testamentary freedom under the Civil and Commercial Code. There is no forced heirship, but a surviving spouse has matrimonial property rights to half of the community property (sin somros).
TH.probateCourtName: ศาลแพ่ง (sān phæ̂ng, Civil Court)
TH.deathRegistrationBody: สำนักงานเขต/อำเภอ (district office)

ID.name: Indonesia
ID.testamentaryFreedom: Complex pluralistic system: Muslims follow Islamic inheritance law (farāʾiḍ) via Religious Courts; ethnic Chinese and certain others follow the Civil Code (Burgerlijk Wetboek) with forced heirship; customary law (adat) applies in other cases.
ID.probateCourtName: Pengadilan Negeri (District Court) / Pengadilan Agama (Religious Court for Muslims)
ID.deathRegistrationBody: Dinas Kependudukan dan Pencatatan Sipil (Population and Civil Registration Office)

AE.name: United Arab Emirates
AE.testamentaryFreedom: Muslim estates are governed by Sharia law with fixed shares (farāʾiḍ); bequests limited to one-third and cannot benefit an existing heir without others' consent. Non-Muslims may opt to apply the law of their nationality or, in ADGM/DIFC, register a will under common law principles.
AE.probateCourtName: محكمة الأحوال الشخصية (maḥkamat al-aḥwāl ash-shakhṣiyyah, Personal Status Court) / DIFC Wills and Probate Registry
AE.deathRegistrationBody: الهيئة الاتحادية للهوية والجنسية (Federal Authority for Identity, Citizenship, Customs and Port Security)

SA.name: Saudi Arabia
SA.testamentaryFreedom: Governed by Islamic inheritance law (farāʾiḍ). Fixed shares for prescribed heirs; bequests (waṣiyyah) limited to one-third of the estate and may not benefit a legal heir without consent of other heirs.
SA.probateCourtName: محكمة الأحوال الشخصية (maḥkamat al-aḥwāl ash-shakhṣiyyah, Personal Status Court)
SA.deathRegistrationBody: وزارة الصحة (Ministry of Health) / الأحوال المدنية (Civil Status Authority)

IL.name: Israel
IL.testamentaryFreedom: Broad testamentary freedom under the Succession Law 1965. No forced heirship, but the surviving spouse has rights to the shared dwelling and maintenance.
IL.probateCourtName: רשם לענייני ירושה (Registrar of Inheritance Affairs) / בית משפט לענייני משפחה (Family Court)

NG.name: Nigeria
NG.testamentaryFreedom: Pluralistic system: common law applies in southern states with broad testamentary freedom; Islamic inheritance law (farāʾiḍ) prevails in northern states; customary law applies in some communities. The applicable system depends on the deceased's domicile, religion, and ethnicity.
NG.probateCourtName: High Court (Probate Division) / Sharia Court of Appeal (in northern states)

ZA.name: South Africa
ZA.testamentaryFreedom: Broad testamentary freedom — no forced heirship. However, the surviving spouse may claim under the Matrimonial Property Act, and a maintenance claim may be made on behalf of dependants.

BR.name: Brazil
BR.testamentaryFreedom: Restricted by legítima (forced heirship). One-half of the estate is reserved for necessary heirs (descendants, ascendants, and surviving spouse). The testator may freely dispose of the other half.
BR.probateCourtName: Vara de Sucessões (Succession Court) / Cartório de Notas (notary office, for extrajudicial inventory)
BR.deathRegistrationBody: Cartório de Registro Civil (Civil Registry Office)
